input.rationale: Sections 9.1 and 9.2 impose symmetrical caps on each party at the greater of $100,000 or twelve months' charges paid, with indemnification payments listed separately in 9.1(a)/9.2(a) and therefore outside the monetary cap, and Section 10 excludes indirect/consequential damages mutually. That satisfies the mutual-cap, 12-months-of-fees and indemnification elements of the fallback. However, the fallback fails on carve-outs: there is no carve-out for breach of confidentiality, gross negligence or willful misconduct, and Section 6 makes matters worse by providing that Sections 5, 9 and 10 prevail over the confidentiality agreement, so confidentiality breaches are capped. We therefore add one mutual carve-out sentence at the fallback level. Preferred items we have not pursued (USD 1,000,000 floor, "paid or payable", data-protection/security, fraud, IP-infringement and payment-obligation carve-outs, including the Section 9.1(c)(2) data-loss exclusion) are noted but not redlined here.

proposal.summary: Carve confidentiality breach, gross negligence and willful misconduct out of the mutual liability caps in Sections 9.1(c) and 9.2(c).
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The mutual $100,000/12-months-of-charges caps are acceptable to us, but our position requires breach of confidentiality obligations, gross negligence and willful misconduct to sit outside the cap, as indemnification payments already do under Sections 9.1(a) and 9.2(a). We have added one mutual carve-out sentence rather than reopening the caps themselves.

ops.text: d. The limitations in Subsections 9.1(c) and 9.2(c) do not apply to damages arising from a party's breach of its confidentiality obligations, its gross negligence, or its willful misconduct.
